Sean —

Thanks for the call this morning. Legal at Acro asked us to get more detail on two items in Exhibit C:

1) The 'pricing slope' callout (Section 2.1) — their counsel wants an explicit formula for how the step discount moves as committed usage ramps. Right now the exhibit has a narrative approach and they want a deterministic equation.

2) Retroactive credit treatment — if we miss a committed threshold in a prior month but then true up on higher volume later in the quarter, they want to know whether credits are applied against future invoices or issued as a refund.

Can you send a redline with the suggested formula and the preferred credit flow? Acro needs this for their procurement review next week.

Ellen —

Thanks — looping in Legal (Marissa) and Finance (Laura) so we can propose firm language. Quick bullets from my side:

- We can replace the narrative in 2.1 with a formula: EffectiveRate = BaseRate * (1 - DiscountCurve(CommittedPct)), where DiscountCurve is a piecewise linear function defined by the commit bands in Exhibit C.
- For retro credits we prefer issuing a credit on the next invoice (applied forward) rather than cash refunds; faster operationally and matches our current billing flows.
- Open to adding an explicit true-up window (quarterly or 30 days) if Acro wants refund rights beyond applied credits.

Marissa/Laura — can you review and I can push a redline (v3) that: a) inserts the formula, b) clarifies credit flow as invoice credit by default, c) includes a 90-day refund trigger if material? Also attaching a quick workbook with sample math.

Next steps: if you confirm language by EOD Monday we can package into a DocuSign-ready order form for Acro's procurement.

Cheers,

All —

Thanks for the context. I drafted a targeted redline to Exhibit C and added two short, trackable paragraphs for: (1) the explicit piecewise formula; and (2) how credits are handled. High-level positions:

- Formula: I used a piecewise linear DiscountCurve with breakpoints at the commit bands in Exhibit C (0-25%, 25-50%, 50-75%, 75%+). The formula block is concise and intended to be unambiguous for downstream billing automation.
- Credits: Default is invoice credit applied to the next billing cycle. For material shortfalls (>10% of quarterly commit) Acro may request a cash refund within 60 days following the quarter close; Redwood reserves the right to offset prior credits against that refund if applicable.
- Audit & Dispute: added a 30-day dispute window for math errors; thereafter numbers become binding.

I've attached OrderForm_ExhibitC_v3_redline.docx (redline mode) and called out three items I'd like commercial sign-off on:

1) Refund threshold (I set 10%) — commercial, please confirm comfortable.
2) Dispute window length (30 days) — finance, please confirm operationally OK.
3) Language on how the DiscountCurve is computed when customer overage occurs mid-quarter.

If commercial approves, I propose we send the redline to Acro as the proposed Exhibit and note that refunds are rare but included for large misses.

Marissa Cole
